hook.line: A long line of dice race games stretches back to Mesopotamia’s “Royal Game of Ur”.
hook.say: Let’s roll through the history of dice!

ch.t: A lineage of dice and racing
p: Backgammon’s relatives — Persian “nard”, Roman “tabula” and more — have been played since ancient times.
In Japan it arrived as “ban-sugoroku”, and gambling on it grew so hot that it was banned.
st: The Royal Game of Ur is buried with kings
Nard appears in tales of royal wit
The name and modern rules settle

ch.say: Popular enough to be banned in Japan!
tl: Ancient race games such as the Royal Game of Ur
“Tabula” is the rage — emperors are said to play
Sugoroku is banned in Japan (Empress Jitō)
The name “backgammon” is recorded in English
The doubling cube is invented in New York
The neural network TD-Gammon nears the world’s best

ch.say: Two dice — dash to the finish!
ch.cap: The starting position; the two sides travel in opposite directions
p: Move by the numbers on two dice; bear all your pieces off first to win.
A lone piece can be “hit” and sent back to the start. Luck and strategy blend perfectly.

ch.say: Names and rules change by country.
cards: Japan’s cousin, played into the Edo era

ch.say: Tap a card to flip it!
cards: A leading theory: “back game” — pieces get sent back
You move that number four times — a big chance

p: A story of dice and people, 4,500 years long.
